_: What agent-seam publishes and how a consumer cuts it. Read here by python/test_closure.py and tools/check-manifest.mjs; read by a consumer's vendor script at vendor time and never at its test time (a consumer's tests run on the digests in its own VENDOR.json). The contract is spec/seam.md + vectors/; each implementation directory re-derives the vectors.

jsRegion._: js/seam.mjs. `start`..`end` (exclusive) is the block the door carries verbatim between its own CANONICAL JSON banner and its `reach-back through a relay` banner; `pinnedMarker`..`start` holds the declarations the door carries verbatim outside that block, matched by name. `sections` are the `// ==== title` banners inside the block, in order; `minLines` is a floor against a mangled banner collapsing the region to nothing.
sections: Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421 subset, verify-only) — T107

python._: python/shared/ is the slice; `verbatimTests` travel with it unchanged into a consumer; `homeTests` exist here in a form that needs no node or relay (core keeps its own variants); `forbiddenImports` is what the closure test refuses.

implementations._skips: Groups this implementation deliberately does NOT check. Its runner asserts each is PRESENT and non-empty in the vectors and prints the skip by name, so the omission is visible: a group nobody loops over is carried in the file, checked by nobody, and indistinguishable from a group that passes. There is no KeyState and no card envelope in this reference to hold to either.

implementations._home: The WordPress plugin (agent-entry-wordpress) VENDORS this directory and adds its own ABSPATH guard as a recorded transform. It is the home; the plugin is a consumer. It lived in the plugin until 2026-09-09, which meant the seam's own suite never ran PHP — so when the JavaScript reference was found accepting a small-order signature on Node 22, whether PHP was exposed was a question about another repository.
